questions.key_step: Turn two ratios of consecutive coefficients into linear equations in n and r.
questions.justification: Two standard ratio equations chained and solved; no insight, options absent but integer answer easy to verify.

questions.key_step: Rewrite (1+x²)⁴(1+x⁴)⁴ via 1-x⁸ or do the 2x+3y+4z=11 casework.
questions.justification: Coefficient extraction from a three-factor product; either a clever identity or careful 4-case count; options available to check.

questions.key_step: Count partitions of 9 into distinct parts.
questions.justification: Small systematic count (8 cases) with a clear reformulation; limited casework.

questions.key_step: Hockey-stick sum, Pascal identity to get m²=51n+1, then smallest m.
questions.justification: Chain of binomial identities followed by a number-theory minimality check; precision needed, no options.
Two standard identities linked (absorption + Vandermonde); a student without these identities faces a long sum.

questions.key_step: Simplify the product of binomials to C(n+p,p)C(n,p-i), apply Vandermonde and sum to 2^(m+n).
questions.justification: Unfamiliar-looking definition, factorial algebra with hidden Vandermonde, then four statements to judge; idea availability is low.

questions.key_step: General-term exponent matching in both expansions; a³ cancels.
questions.justification: Same task as the anchor 2023-P1-Q13 (L4): find both coefficients by exponent matching and equate; slip-prone with no options.

questions.key_step: Recognise a_j as terms of (1+2/5)^23 and use the greatest-term formula.
questions.justification: Official 2025 question, rated 4 in the bank (largest coefficient in (1+2x/5)^23).
